content_html:
English · 한국어

Author, validate, serve and collect live values for AAS (Asset Administration Shell) — in one web app. Upload one machine's AASX, see exactly which rules it breaks, and fix what can be fixed in one step.

This used to take three tools. VEXPLOR AAS Studio brings the work together and is built so that people new to AAS can follow along.

Task Usual tool Here
Open · edit · export AASX AASX Package Explorer (desktop) In the browser, with findings and auto-fix
Serve AAS to other systems (Part 2 REST · registry) Eclipse BaSyx server The same server does it
Collect machine values · publish them by subscription Separate OPC UA client/server Collects per the AID in the AAS and publishes via an OPC UA server

Not affiliated with, and not derived from, the tools above — it combines the same jobs in one place.

New here? Click "Start with a sample" on the start screen to open a fully filled equipment file and a process structure.

Website: wace.me/en-platform-aas-studio

Docs: Usage · Install · Deployment & hosting · The 52 rules · Using it with Logic Studio — every document is also available in Korean.

Why

AAS is in place as a standard. Putting it into a factory is still work left outside the specification.

A review of ten years of AAS research (IEEE Access, 2025) names integration with existing machines and systems as a key challenge holding back adoption. Several studies point to the effort of building an AAS by hand, and the open tools are split into editors, servers and libraries, so collecting field values means mapping it yourself in configuration files. VEXPLOR AAS Studio lets software take on that work, so an AAS does not end as a document but becomes operating data with live values from the machines on the floor.

What people hit on the floor In VEXPLOR AAS Studio
Attaching to machines and PLCs that already run Collects from OPC UA, Modbus TCP and MQTT per the AID in the AAS, and reads S7, MELSEC (MC protocol) and LS ELECTRIC XGT PLCs directly — read only, a VEXPLOR extension binding. The remote collector sends outward only; PLC programs are not changed
Building an AAS by hand Start from a filled sample, fill values at once from tables or CSV; 52 rules point out problems and 19 fix them automatically
One tool per job Open, edit, check, Part 2 REST, field value collection and OPC UA publishing in one screen
Passing the standard, failing the receiver Checks the Korean receiving validator's (KOSMO Validator) business rules — semantic ID allow-list, mandatory submodels, package structure — before submission, and shows conflicts with the standard as a policy the user decides

There are real line deployments (Bosch Rexroth and others). They adopted AAS to end months of integration work whenever machines change — and they too report that creating the AAS itself is the first hurdle for many users. Evidence and sources: docs/background.md.

The receiving validator remains the only authority on acceptance. This tool is a pre-check.

What it does
Open & edit Load AASX (JSON or XML), browse it as a tree, edit values, elements, submodels and concept descriptions. Fill many values at once from a submodel value table or from a CSV equipment list
Lint 52 rules in three layers — package structure (L1), metamodel constraints (L2), submission business rules (L3)
Auto-fix Preview the fixable findings (19 rules), choose, apply at once. Every relocation is recorded
Report A printable HTML validation report
What to fill With the IDTA templates installed, every value row shows required · collected · optional, and "Show only what to fill" hides the rest
Undo & history One-step undo, and restore a submodel to an earlier point
Types and units Split a type file into units; when the type changes, review the differences line by line and pull only the lines you choose — values edited on site are never overwritten
Process bundles Company → line → process → equipment → part. Group machines into a process and export a submission bundle
Data collection Read live values from OPC UA · Modbus TCP · MQTT devices, and directly from S7, MELSEC (MC protocol) and LS ELECTRIC XGT PLCs — read only, a VEXPLOR extension binding not yet checked on real PLCs — addressed by the AID submodel inside the AAS. Each value shows whether it is live, stale or missing, and each machine gets a daily status bar (running · stopped · alarm). Add dozens of tags from one pattern
Standard API IDTA Part 2 REST API, so other systems can read the AAS held here
MES · ERP · CMMS integration A pull feed of every change and runtime event (CloudEvents), signed webhooks and MQTT, equipment / BOM / hierarchy / maintenance / document exports in JSON or CSV, ERP numbers kept next to the AASX, and server-side state, alarm, counter and threshold rules. A secure OPC UA server (accounts + encryption). See docs/integration.md
Accounts Admin / editor / viewer, with an audit trail of who changed what
English & Korean, light & dark The interface and everything the server writes — findings, rule descriptions, the validation report, bundle README, errors — come in English or Korean. If you never choose, the browser language decides (Korean browser → Korean, anything else → English). Light and dark themes

What's new in 2.3 – 2.12

Feature Release Detail
Empty list elements in XML read as empty lists 2.12.1 A list closed with no items (<qualifiers />, <description />, a collection's <value /> …) was read as the empty string. In KOSMO's 179 public reference models the check then stopped part way in 45 files and a saved copy could not be opened again for 27; both are now 0. The empty list is kept as it was and reported by PKG-EMPTY-ARRAY (auto-fix). scripts/lint.mjs now checks each file by its own metamodel version and looks into subfolders. New guide: using KOSMO reference models with a file-by-file table
Range limits in tag hints 2.12.0 A Range element with the same semanticId as a tag's value now gives limits too — its min as lsl, its max as usl — so a receiver such as Logic Studio gets lower specification limits from the file. Limits from the KOSMO property pairs come first, ranges after; a tag may carry several of the same bound, each with its source, for a person to choose. No schema change. The KOSMO model files in use today hold no Range, so their hints are unchanged; for a lower limit, add a Range with the value's semanticId and an idShort different from the value's (integration)
LS ELECTRIC XGT, read directly 2.11.0 XGK · XGI · XGR · XGB PLCs with an FEnet module are read over the XGT dedicated protocol (TCP 2004) without a gateway — read only. Addresses are written as XG5000 shows them (D100, D100.3, P0001A, %MW100, %IX0.0.3). AID 1.1 has no XGT binding, so this is a VEXPLOR extension binding marked by our binding IRI. Built from LS ELECTRIC's published FEnet manual and tested against a test server built from it — not yet checked on a real PLC; please send a PLC field report. The server reads it with COLLECT=on, the remote collector from VEXPLOR Edge 1.3.0 — usage §8
XGT in the edge contract · PLC field report 2.11.0 The read list's protocol adds XGT; the contract stays vexplor.edge/1. An older edge reports XGT is not read by this edge yet and keeps reading the others. A new issue form collects real-PLC results for S7, MC and XGT. Webhooks and MQTT subscriptions now also refuse port 2004 unless the allow entry names it
S7 and MC protocol, read directly 2.10.0 Siemens S7-300 / 400 / 1200 / 1500 (ISO-on-TCP) and MELSEC Q · L · iQ-R · iQ-F (MC protocol 3E binary) are read without a gateway — read only. Addresses are written as the engineering tool shows them (DB10.DBD4:REAL, D100, D10.3). AID 1.1 has no binding for either, so this is a VEXPLOR extension binding, marked by our binding IRI; other AID tools do not read these interfaces. Tested against test servers built from the published formats — not yet checked on real PLCs. The server reads them with COLLECT=on, and the remote collector from VEXPLOR Edge 1.2.0 — usage §8
Remote collector on Windows 2.10.0 Settings → Remote collectors → "+ Connect a collector" has a Linux and a Windows tab. The Windows tab gives one line for Command Prompt or PowerShell (run as administrator) that downloads, checks the hash, installs and starts the Windows service — it changes no execution policy. Needs VEXPLOR Edge 1.2.0 or later (Windows x64), whose service install is tested on GitHub's Windows runners; not yet on a factory PC — remote collector install
S7 and MC in the edge contract 2.10.0 The read list's protocol adds S7 and MC; the contract stays vexplor.edge/1. An edge older than 1.2.0 does not read such an interface, reports why (S7 is not read by this edge yet) and keeps reading the others — contract §4
AAS metamodel V3.0 · V3.1 · V3.2 2.9.0 Opens files of all three versions — an XML file by its namespace, a JSON file (no version marker) by the lowest version that holds its content — and remembers the version each file came in as. Download AASX writes that version unless you pick another; new equipment, samples and passport templates are V3.1, the version KOSMO asks for. Writing a lower version lists every field it leaves out, with its value, and refuses values it cannot express (assetKind Role or Batch, a missing entityType …) unless you tick "download with the values as they are". V3.1 · V3.2 output is checked against the official JSON schemas in the tests — the official validator aas-test-engines 1.0.3 checks V3.0 only. Usage §4-10
Product passport (DPP) templates and checks 2.9.0 "Start from a product passport (DPP) template" on the start screen opens one of eight IDTA templates as published (CC BY 4.0): DPP Part 1 metadata (IDTA 02099-1 1.0.2) and the seven parts of the battery passport (IDTA 02035-1 – 7). Rules DPP-1 – DPP-5 check the passport metadata: the seven mandatory items, granularity (Model · Item · Batch), lastUpdate in UTC, content specification ids, and granularity against the shell's assetKind. This supports writing and checking passport data; it is not a verdict on conformity with the EU DPP regulation
Checks follow the file's version 2.9.0 52 rules, up from 44. AASd-090 and AASd-120, removed in V3.1, apply to V3.0 files only; PKG-FILE-URI and the idShort pattern follow each version's official schema; new AASd-137 · AASd-138 for V3.2 and PKG-MM-VERSION for content the declared version cannot hold (a V3.2 Batch in a V3.0 file). Below V3.2, AASd-119/129 now also look inside Operation variables
Korean and spaced attachment names in V3.1 · V3.2 2.9.0 Those versions accept only URIs as attachment paths. Downloading as V3.1 or V3.2 percent-encodes such names in the model and in the package parts, relationships and content types, so the reference still finds the file; this tool shows the original name. V3.0 output is unchanged
Part 2 under /api/v3 2.9.0 Clients generated from the V3.1 · V3.2 OpenAPI call /api/v3/…; the same routes answer there as under /api/v3.0. Endpoints new in V3.2 ($recent-changes, $history, $signed, asynchronous packages) answer 404
XML files read as written 2.9.0 Comparing the official examples' XML with their JSON found four reading faults, V3.0 files included: Range min and max were read as false (both bounds lost), an empty <administration/> as an empty string, an OperationVariable value as a one-item list, and the V3.2 unit data specification was not recognised. A file uploaded as XML before 2.9.0 keeps what was read then — upload it again
Remote collector intake, faster and whole 2.8.1 A batch from a remote collector is one write to the database: the values of every file in it and the record that it arrived go in one transaction, so a batch is stored whole or not at all. Before, each value was its own write, which capped a 4-core test server near 11,500 values a second with the database half idle; the same server now takes about 50,000. The remote collector list reads each file once per request instead of once per collector, and approving one collector writes only that collector. PG_POOL_MAX sets the number of database connections (default 10) — install
Server status while the database is down 2.8.1 With the database stopped or overloaded, "Server status" answered after more than 10 seconds or not at all. It now answers within about 7 seconds and shows the store connection as failed
Security and login on collection links 2.8.0 "Create collection link" picks the OPC UA security mode (Sign · SignAndEncrypt) and policy, and "Login required" for OPC UA and MQTT. The user name and password never go into the equipment file — they stay in the server's credentials file and the factory PC's credentials.json, keyed by the endpoint. "Load from equipment" connects with the chosen security and login. An old MQTT link with a password in its address is left out of the remote collector list and rule AID-1 says so (MQTT login needs VEXPLOR Edge 1.1.0 or later)
Why a read failed is kept 2.8.0 Automatic collection and remote collectors store the reason with the value. The row keeps "Read failed — reason" after the screen is opened again, and Modbus and MQTT, which have no quality code, show it too
Units, Modbus order, read period 2.8.0 A unit on every tag row, byte and word order (ABCD · CDAB · BADC · DCBA) on Modbus rows and a read period per machine, all on the screen. Remote collectors read at that period, and "Edit link" opens filled in with the current link
Collector health and server status 2.8.0 Each row of the remote collector list carries the server's OK · Warning · Problem badge and its reason in one line (free disk space, failed sending, clock offset, read success rate, queue, silence, no equipment connected). "Show state" opens the factory PC (CPU, memory, disk, uptime, clock offset), the line to the server, response time, success rate and reconnects per equipment, and the last 24 hours (values sent by VEXPLOR Edge 1.1.0 or later). Admins see the server's own state in Settings (store connection, disk, batches of the last hour, version). Usage §8-8
One-click remote collector 2.7.0 Settings → Remote collectors → "+ Connect a collector" — check the server address and the read list, press one button, and you get one line to paste on the factory Linux PC. That line downloads, checks the hash, installs, registers and approves; the screen turns to "Receiving" the moment the PC connects. The same screen shows the last batch, values received and machine connections, and pauses, resumes or revokes. Admins turn remote collection on right there (servers with EDGE empty)
VEXPLOR Edge, its own open source 2.7.0 The remote collector now ships from its own repository waceinc/vexplor-edge (Apache-2.0) with its own version (1.0.0). The canonical contract vexplor.edge/1 lives there; this server receives it as is
Collect pane refreshes itself 2.7.0 With a file that has a collection link open, values come in every 10 s, and while a remote collector's values arrive the connection shows "Receiving"
Equipment reader libraries 2.7.0 The release packages add @aas/collector, @aas/fieldbus and @aas/opcua — the remote collector reads OPC UA, Modbus TCP and MQTT with exactly this server's code
Remote collector (VEXPLOR Edge) 2.3.0 One program on the factory PC reads PLCs and sends signed batches out over HTTPS — read only, outbound only. Linux x64 · arm64 (install); Windows x64 from 2.10.0 · Edge 1.2.0
Send changes only 2.4.0 OPC UA subscriptions with a deadband. Measured 6 tags · 1 s · 5 min: 283 KB polling → 88 KB
Values from an outage 2.3.0 Batches read while the link was down are sent oldest first and kept up to maxQueueDays (default 30)
Factory server install 2.4.0 One command puts AAS Studio, the database and the remote collector on one Linux server; it comes back after a reboot (site install)
Compression · aggregates 2.4.0 With TimescaleDB Community Edition: values older than 7 days are compressed, 1-minute and 1-hour aggregates are built. Measured 1,000 tags · 1 s · 1 h: 1,099 MB → 50 MB
Logic Studio guide 2.6.0 ? Help → Use it in VEXPLOR Logic Studio and docs/logic-studio.md: download the checked AASX, drop it on Logic Studio Cloud's equipment screen, and it becomes the equipment register — nothing to install or convert
Tag hints 2.5.0 Each read-list tag names its model element's semanticId, a suggested role (state · counter · alarm · meter · condition · quality) and limits from the same file, so a receiver such as Logic Studio pre-fills roles and SPC limits for a person to confirm (contract §4.1)
Read list without a server 2.3.0 aidReadList in @aas/bundle turns the AID inside an AASX into the tag list a collector reads — no AID parser needed in other products

Full notes: Releases.

Works with VEXPLOR Logic Studio

AASX files authored and checked here import straight into VEXPLOR Logic Studio (WACE's factory platform — MES · PLM · ERP · QMS) — nothing to install in the factory, no conversion step.

  1. Author the equipment AASX here and pass the 52-rule check.
  2. Drop the file on the equipment screen of Logic Studio Cloud.
  3. Check types, equipment, plant and line in the preview, then import — each machine enters the equipment register linked to its type.
  • Type files and Instance files are imported separately.
  • Dropping the same file again ends with "Nothing changes" — no duplicate equipment.
  • Step-by-step guide: docs/logic-studio.md. The in-app help (? Help) has the same steps.
  • Live values are in preparation: the same remote collector is being prepared to send machine values to Logic Studio Cloud as well. The two endpoints any receiver implements are in docs/edge-contract.md. Not offered yet.

Quick start

Docker

git clone <this repository> && cd <folder>
cp .env.example .env          # only POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required
docker compose up -d --build

Open http://localhost:8080. Details: install.md. A factory server with no internet: the site install bundle, site-install.md.

The database image timescale/timescaledb is TimescaleDB Community Edition by Tiger Data, under the Timescale License (https://www.tigerdata.com/legal/licenses) — not under this repository's licence; Docker pulls it from Docker Hub on your machine. -oss images are TimescaleDB Apache-2 Edition (no compression or continuous aggregates).

From source — Node.js 24 LTS (22 or later works)

npm install
npx tsc -b
npm run build --workspace apps/web
node apps/api/dist/server.js     # http://localhost:8080

With no configuration the server binds to 127.0.0.1 only. To share it, configure accounts or an API key first — see Usage §12.

Create the first administrator right after starting (Settings → Create the first administrator). Once any account exists, both the UI and the API require a login (or an API key). Until then the server is open.

For development, run the UI separately:

npm run dev:api     # API on 8080
npm run dev:web     # UI on 5173 (in another terminal)

Layout

A TypeScript monorepo — one language for the front end and the server.

Package Role
packages/aas-core AAS metamodel types (V3.0 · V3.1 · V3.2) and version conversion · server-side text in English and Korean
packages/aasx AASX (OPC package) reader/writer with lossless round-trip
packages/linter Rules, auto-fixes, reports
packages/store Storage — in-memory, folder and PostgreSQL pass the same conformance suite
packages/collector Resolves AID and collects field values
packages/opcua OPC UA client and server (node-opcua)
packages/fieldbus Modbus TCP · MQTT · S7 · MC · XGT protocol collection adapters, read only (no external dependencies — node:net) · test device and broker
apps/api REST API server
apps/web React front end

Using the libraries in another product

@aas/core, @aas/aasx, @aas/linter, @aas/bundle (the integration bundle built from AASX files without a server — buildBundle) and @aas/collector, @aas/fieldbus, @aas/opcua (equipment readers — the remote collector uses them) are attached to each GitHub release as npm tarballs (node scripts/pack-libraries.mjs, checksums in SHA256SUMS). Install them by release URL:

"@aas/aasx": "https://github.com/waceinc/vexplor-aas/releases/download/v2.12.1/aas-aasx-2.12.1.tgz"

Never by version number — the @aas scope on the public npm registry is not ours, so "@aas/core": "^2.0.0" would install whatever someone else publishes there. The tarballs point at each other by release URL, so one pinned URL is enough.

Remote collector

When the server is outside the factory (cloud, head office), put VEXPLOR Edge on one factory PC — its own open source, waceinc/vexplor-edge. It reads only the PLCs of an approved list and sends signed batches out over HTTPS — outbound only, no remote stop. Connecting is one button and one pasted line under Settings → Remote collectors → "+ Connect a collector" (Linux x64 · arm64; Windows x64 from VEXPLOR Edge 1.2.0). This server's side: docs/edge-install.md; the contract copy: docs/edge-contract.md.

Standards

Standard Status
AAS metamodel V3.0 · V3.1 · V3.2 (IDTA-01001-3-0 · 3-1 · 3-2) Reads all three. A file is downloaded as the version it came in as (an XML namespace says it; a JSON file carries no version, so the lowest version that holds its content). New models — new equipment, samples, the passport templates — are V3.1, the version KOSMO asks for. Another version can be picked when downloading: writing a lower one lists the fields it leaves out and refuses values it cannot express
Checking a written file V3.0: the official validator aas-test-engines 1.0.3, which checks V3.0 only. V3.1 · V3.2: the official JSON schemas of admin-shell-io/aas-specs-metamodel (v3.1.2 · v3.2.0) in this repository's tests — aas-test-engines does not check those versions yet
AASX package (IDTA-01005) Reads JSON and XML, writes JSON. For V3.1 · V3.2, attachment names with spaces or non-ASCII letters are percent-encoded (RFC 3986, UTF-8) together with their parts and relationships — those versions accept only URIs
Part 2 REST API (IDTA-01002-3-0) AasxFileServer 6/6 · ConceptDescription 7/7 · AAS Repository 47/54 · Submodel Repository 38/45 · partial Registry and Discovery. Served under /api/v3.0 and, for V3.1 · V3.2 clients, /api/v3 (same routes). Endpoints new in V3.2 ($recent-changes, $history, $signed, asynchronous package operations) are not implemented and answer 404
AID 1.1 (IDTA-02017) OPC UA · Modbus TCP · MQTT address resolution (Modbus · MQTT use the W3C WoT binding notation). S7, MC and XGT are not AID bindings — a VEXPLOR extension in the standard base / href places, marked by our binding IRI (docs/usage.md §8)

node scripts/part2-coverage.mjs compares the implementation against the specification's OpenAPI files and prints the exact coverage.

Protocols

Protocol Equipment Server (COLLECT=on) Remote collector (VEXPLOR Edge) Basis
OPC UA Any OPC UA server Yes Yes AID 1.1
Modbus TCP Modbus TCP devices Yes Yes AID 1.1 (W3C WoT binding notation)
MQTT MQTT brokers Yes Yes AID 1.1 (W3C WoT binding notation)
S7 (ISO-on-TCP, S7comm) Siemens S7-300 · 400 · 1200 · 1500 Yes (2.10.0) Edge 1.2.0 or later VEXPLOR extension binding — tested against test servers only. Real PLC: waiting for user reports (field report)
MC protocol (3E binary) MELSEC Q · L · iQ-R · iQ-F Yes (2.10.0) Edge 1.2.0 or later VEXPLOR extension binding — tested against test servers only. Real PLC: waiting for user reports (field report)
XGT dedicated protocol (FEnet, TCP 2004) LS ELECTRIC XGK · XGI · XGR · XGB Yes (2.11.0) Edge 1.3.0 or later VEXPLOR extension binding, built from LS ELECTRIC's published FEnet manual — tested against test servers only. Real PLC: waiting for user reports (field report)

Checked on a real PLC? Not yet for S7, MC and XGT. They are built from the published specifications and tested against test servers that follow them — no real PLC was available. If you read one of these PLCs, please tell us what you saw with the PLC field report: maker, series, CPU, firmware, address, the value you expected and the value read (or the reason it could not be read). Each report goes into this table.

XGT: check the word order first. LS ELECTRIC's manuals do not say in which order the words of a value over several words (DINT, REAL, LREAL …) are placed; this tool reads the low word first. If INT and BOOL read right but REAL or DINT read wrong, that is the reason — a field report with both values settles it. The other open points from the manuals are listed in usage §8 (XGT, "What the published manuals do not settle").

All of them are read only. HTTP and BACnet interfaces in an AID are recognised but not collected.

Using KOSMO reference models

KOSMO publishes AAS reference models per equipment type from the Korean manufacturing-data standardization programme at github.com/kosmo-AAS — the files are in kosmo-AAS/kasmo-AAS_Pubilc (the repository's own spelling). KOSMO submissions ask for metamodel V3.1; the published files themselves declare V3.0.

  1. Download the reference model for your machine from that repository.
  2. Open it in AAS Studio — the XML body is converted to JSON on import.
  3. Check against the KOSMO submission rules: filter the findings by L3, apply auto-fix where offered (usage §4-8).
  4. Fill in the machine's values — most findings are empty Property values the model leaves for you (usage §4-3).
  5. Download as V3.1 (usage §4-10). One-letter idShorts (Q, T, X …) are valid in V3.0 but not in V3.1, so the download window refuses them — rename them first.

Measured 2026-10-20 against commit 6f6ac69 of that repository with AAS Studio 2.12.1:

Item Result
Files 179 AASX — all open, all declare metamodel V3.0
Check ran to the end on all 179 (2.12.0 stopped on 45 files with empty list elements such as <qualifiers /> — fixed in 2.12.1)
Findings (179 files) L1 errors 12,182 · L2 errors 48,117 · L3 errors 152,445. Of all errors, 64,357 are empty Property values (KOSMO-SME-4) and 146,106 are auto-fixable. Most frequent: KOSMO-SME-4 · AASd-121~128 · KOSMO-CD-2 · KOSMO-CD-4 · KOSMO-SME-5
Round trip 179 the same — every saved copy opens again
Export as V3.1 156 written with 0 dropped values; 23 refused (one-letter idShorts). 33 of the 156 pass the official V3.1 schema — the rest fail on values in the source: empty lists (minItems 1), empty text, units or idShorts

Every file, rule by rule: docs/kosmo-compat.md. License: that repository shows no license, so this repository does not include its files — it only links to them. Check the provider's terms before redistributing them.

Things to know

  • Authentication is opt-in. With neither accounts nor an API key the server only listens on the local machine.
  • The OPC UA server (port 4840) requires an account and encryption (Sign / SignAndEncrypt). It is off by default; OPCUA_ALLOW_INSECURE=on restores the old unauthenticated port for isolated test networks only.
  • Once people sign in, put HTTPS in front — see Caddyfile.example.
  • In English, what stays as it was written is what comes from your own files (names, values) and the folder names of the submission bundle, which the submission format fixes.
  • Server startup logs are Korean by default; set AAS_LANG=en for English.
  • Report security problems through the channel in SECURITY.md, not a public issue.

Contributing

bash scripts/ci.sh      # build → typecheck → tests → spec coverage → generated docs → licenses → i18n

CI runs on Node.js 22 and 24. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

What people hit on the floor In VEXPLOR AAS Studio Attaching to machines and PLCs that already run Collects from OPC UA, Modbus TCP and MQTT per the AID in the AAS, and reads S7, MELSEC (MC protocol) and LS ELECTRIC XGT PLCs directly — read only, a VEXPLOR extension binding. The remote collector sends outward only; PLC programs are not changed Building an AAS by hand Start from a filled sample, fill values at once from tables or CSV; 52 rules point out problems and 19 fix them automatically One tool per job Open, edit, check, Part 2 REST, field value collection and OPC UA publishing in one screen Passing the standard, failing the receiver Checks the Korean receiving validator's (KOSMO Validator) business rules — semantic ID allow-list, mandatory submodels, package structure — before submission, and shows conflicts with the standard as a policy the user decides There are real line deployments (Bosch Rexroth and others). They adopted AAS to end months of integration work whenever machines change — and they too report that creating the AAS itself is the first hurdle for many users. Evidence and sources: docs/background.md. The receiving validator remains the only authority on acceptance. This tool is a pre-check. What it does Open & edit Load AASX (JSON or XML), browse it as a tree, edit values, elements, submodels and concept descriptions. Fill many values at once from a submodel value table or from a CSV equipment list Lint 52 rules in three layers — package structure (L1), metamodel constraints (L2), submission business rules (L3) Auto-fix Preview the fixable findings (19 rules), choose, apply at once. Every relocation is recorded Report A printable HTML validation report What to fill With the IDTA templates installed, every value row shows required · collected · optional, and "Show only what to fill" hides the rest Undo & history One-step undo, and restore a submodel to an earlier point Types and units Split a type file into units; when the type changes, review the differences line by line and pull only the lines you choose — values edited on site are never overwritten Process bundles Company → line → process → equipment → part. Group machines into a process and export a submission bundle Data collection Read live values from OPC UA · Modbus TCP · MQTT devices, and directly from S7, MELSEC (MC protocol) and LS ELECTRIC XGT PLCs — read only, a VEXPLOR extension binding not yet checked on real PLCs — addressed by the AID submodel inside the AAS. Each value shows whether it is live, stale or missing, and each machine gets a daily status bar (running · stopped · alarm). Add dozens of tags from one pattern Standard API IDTA Part 2 REST API, so other systems can read the AAS held here MES · ERP · CMMS integration A pull feed of every change and runtime event (CloudEvents), signed webhooks and MQTT, equipment / BOM / hierarchy / maintenance / document exports in JSON or CSV, ERP numbers kept next to the AASX, and server-side state, alarm, counter and threshold rules. A secure OPC UA server (accounts + encryption). See docs/integration.md Accounts Admin / editor / viewer, with an audit trail of who changed what English & Korean, light & dark The interface and everything the server writes — findings, rule descriptions, the validation report, bundle README, errors — come in English or Korean. If you never choose, the browser language decides (Korean browser → Korean, anything else → English). Light and dark themes What's new in 2.3 – 2.12 Feature Release Detail Empty list elements in XML read as empty lists 2.12.1 A list closed with no items (<qualifiers />, <description />, a collection's <value /> …) was read as the empty string. In KOSMO's 179 public reference models the check then stopped part way in 45 files and a saved copy could not be opened again for 27; both are now 0. The empty list is kept as it was and reported by PKG-EMPTY-ARRAY (auto-fix). scripts/lint.mjs now checks each file by its own metamodel version and looks into subfolders. New guide: using KOSMO reference models with a file-by-file table Range limits in tag hints 2.12.0 A Range element with the same semanticId as a tag's value now gives limits too — its min as lsl, its max as usl — so a receiver such as Logic Studio gets lower specification limits from the file. Limits from the KOSMO property pairs come first, ranges after; a tag may carry several of the same bound, each with its source, for a person to choose. No schema change. The KOSMO model files in use today hold no Range, so their hints are unchanged; for a lower limit, add a Range with the value's semanticId and an idShort different from the value's (integration) LS ELECTRIC XGT, read directly 2.11.0 XGK · XGI · XGR · XGB PLCs with an FEnet module are read over the XGT dedicated protocol (TCP 2004) without a gateway — read only. Addresses are written as XG5000 shows them (D100, D100.3, P0001A, %MW100, %IX0.0.3). AID 1.1 has no XGT binding, so this is a VEXPLOR extension binding marked by our binding IRI. Built from LS ELECTRIC's published FEnet manual and tested against a test server built from it — not yet checked on a real PLC; please send a PLC field report. The server reads it with COLLECT=on, the remote collector from VEXPLOR Edge 1.3.0 — usage §8 XGT in the edge contract · PLC field report 2.11.0 The read list's protocol adds XGT; the contract stays vexplor.edge/1. An older edge reports XGT is not read by this edge yet and keeps reading the others. A new issue form collects real-PLC results for S7, MC and XGT. Webhooks and MQTT subscriptions now also refuse port 2004 unless the allow entry names it S7 and MC protocol, read directly 2.10.0 Siemens S7-300 / 400 / 1200 / 1500 (ISO-on-TCP) and MELSEC Q · L · iQ-R · iQ-F (MC protocol 3E binary) are read without a gateway — read only. Addresses are written as the engineering tool shows them (DB10.DBD4:REAL, D100, D10.3). AID 1.1 has no binding for either, so this is a VEXPLOR extension binding, marked by our binding IRI; other AID tools do not read these interfaces. Tested against test servers built from the published formats — not yet checked on real PLCs. The server reads them with COLLECT=on, and the remote collector from VEXPLOR Edge 1.2.0 — usage §8 Remote collector on Windows 2.10.0 Settings → Remote collectors → "+ Connect a collector" has a Linux and a Windows tab. The Windows tab gives one line for Command Prompt or PowerShell (run as administrator) that downloads, checks the hash, installs and starts the Windows service — it changes no execution policy. Needs VEXPLOR Edge 1.2.0 or later (Windows x64), whose service install is tested on GitHub's Windows runners; not yet on a factory PC — remote collector install S7 and MC in the edge contract 2.10.0 The read list's protocol adds S7 and MC; the contract stays vexplor.edge/1. An edge older than 1.2.0 does not read such an interface, reports why (S7 is not read by this edge yet) and keeps reading the others — contract §4 AAS metamodel V3.0 · V3.1 · V3.2 2.9.0 Opens files of all three versions — an XML file by its namespace, a JSON file (no version marker) by the lowest version that holds its content — and remembers the version each file came in as. Download AASX writes that version unless you pick another; new equipment, samples and passport templates are V3.1, the version KOSMO asks for. Writing a lower version lists every field it leaves out, with its value, and refuses values it cannot express (assetKind Role or Batch, a missing entityType …) unless you tick "download with the values as they are". V3.1 · V3.2 output is checked against the official JSON schemas in the tests — the official validator aas-test-engines 1.0.3 checks V3.0 only. Usage §4-10 Product passport (DPP) templates and checks 2.9.0 "Start from a product passport (DPP) template" on the start screen opens one of eight IDTA templates as published (CC BY 4.0): DPP Part 1 metadata (IDTA 02099-1 1.0.2) and the seven parts of the battery passport (IDTA 02035-1 – 7). Rules DPP-1 – DPP-5 check the passport metadata: the seven mandatory items, granularity (Model · Item · Batch), lastUpdate in UTC, content specification ids, and granularity against the shell's assetKind. This supports writing and checking passport data; it is not a verdict on conformity with the EU DPP regulation Checks follow the file's version 2.9.0 52 rules, up from 44. AASd-090 and AASd-120, removed in V3.1, apply to V3.0 files only; PKG-FILE-URI and the idShort pattern follow each version's official schema; new AASd-137 · AASd-138 for V3.2 and PKG-MM-VERSION for content the declared version cannot hold (a V3.2 Batch in a V3.0 file). Below V3.2, AASd-119/129 now also look inside Operation variables Korean and spaced attachment names in V3.1 · V3.2 2.9.0 Those versions accept only URIs as attachment paths. Downloading as V3.1 or V3.2 percent-encodes such names in the model and in the package parts, relationships and content types, so the reference still finds the file; this tool shows the original name. V3.0 output is unchanged Part 2 under /api/v3 2.9.0 Clients generated from the V3.1 · V3.2 OpenAPI call /api/v3/…; the same routes answer there as under /api/v3.0. Endpoints new in V3.2 ($recent-changes, $history, $signed, asynchronous packages) answer 404 XML files read as written 2.9.0 Comparing the official examples' XML with their JSON found four reading faults, V3.0 files included: Range min and max were read as false (both bounds lost), an empty <administration/> as an empty string, an OperationVariable value as a one-item list, and the V3.2 unit data specification was not recognised. A file uploaded as XML before 2.9.0 keeps what was read then — upload it again Remote collector intake, faster and whole 2.8.1 A batch from a remote collector is one write to the database: the values of every file in it and the record that it arrived go in one transaction, so a batch is stored whole or not at all. Before, each value was its own write, which capped a 4-core test server near 11,500 values a second with the database half idle; the same server now takes about 50,000. The remote collector list reads each file once per request instead of once per collector, and approving one collector writes only that collector. PG_POOL_MAX sets the number of database connections (default 10) — install Server status while the database is down 2.8.1 With the database stopped or overloaded, "Server status" answered after more than 10 seconds or not at all. It now answers within about 7 seconds and shows the store connection as failed Security and login on collection links 2.8.0 "Create collection link" picks the OPC UA security mode (Sign · SignAndEncrypt) and policy, and "Login required" for OPC UA and MQTT. The user name and password never go into the equipment file — they stay in the server's credentials file and the factory PC's credentials.json, keyed by the endpoint. "Load from equipment" connects with the chosen security and login. An old MQTT link with a password in its address is left out of the remote collector list and rule AID-1 says so (MQTT login needs VEXPLOR Edge 1.1.0 or later) Why a read failed is kept 2.8.0 Automatic collection and remote collectors store the reason with the value. The row keeps "Read failed — reason" after the screen is opened again, and Modbus and MQTT, which have no quality code, show it too Units, Modbus order, read period 2.8.0 A unit on every tag row, byte and word order (ABCD · CDAB · BADC · DCBA) on Modbus rows and a read period per machine, all on the screen. Remote collectors read at that period, and "Edit link" opens filled in with the current link Collector health and server status 2.8.0 Each row of the remote collector list carries the server's OK · Warning · Problem badge and its reason in one line (free disk space, failed sending, clock offset, read success rate, queue, silence, no equipment connected). "Show state" opens the factory PC (CPU, memory, disk, uptime, clock offset), the line to the server, response time, success rate and reconnects per equipment, and the last 24 hours (values sent by VEXPLOR Edge 1.1.0 or later). Admins see the server's own state in Settings (store connection, disk, batches of the last hour, version). Usage §8-8 One-click remote collector 2.7.0 Settings → Remote collectors → "+ Connect a collector" — check the server address and the read list, press one button, and you get one line to paste on the factory Linux PC. That line downloads, checks the hash, installs, registers and approves; the screen turns to "Receiving" the moment the PC connects. The same screen shows the last batch, values received and machine connections, and pauses, resumes or revokes. Admins turn remote collection on right there (servers with EDGE empty) VEXPLOR Edge, its own open source 2.7.0 The remote collector now ships from its own repository waceinc/vexplor-edge (Apache-2.0) with its own version (1.0.0). The canonical contract vexplor.edge/1 lives there; this server receives it as is Collect pane refreshes itself 2.7.0 With a file that has a collection link open, values come in every 10 s, and while a remote collector's values arrive the connection shows "Receiving" Equipment reader libraries 2.7.0 The release packages add @aas/collector, @aas/fieldbus and @aas/opcua — the remote collector reads OPC UA, Modbus TCP and MQTT with exactly this server's code Remote collector (VEXPLOR Edge) 2.3.0 One program on the factory PC reads PLCs and sends signed batches out over HTTPS — read only, outbound only. Linux x64 · arm64 (install); Windows x64 from 2.10.0 · Edge 1.2.0 Send changes only 2.4.0 OPC UA subscriptions with a deadband. Measured 6 tags · 1 s · 5 min: 283 KB polling → 88 KB Values from an outage 2.3.0 Batches read while the link was down are sent oldest first and kept up to maxQueueDays (default 30) Factory server install 2.4.0 One command puts AAS Studio, the database and the remote collector on one Linux server; it comes back after a reboot (site install) Compression · aggregates 2.4.0 With TimescaleDB Community Edition: values older than 7 days are compressed, 1-minute and 1-hour aggregates are built. They are built from the published specifications and tested against test servers that follow them — no real PLC was available. If you read one of these PLCs, please tell us what you saw with the PLC field report: maker, series, CPU, firmware, address, the value you expected and the value read (or the reason it could not be read). Each report goes into this table. XGT: check the word order first. LS ELECTRIC's manuals do not say in which order the words of a value over several words (DINT, REAL, LREAL …) are placed; this tool reads the low word first. If INT and BOOL read right but REAL or DINT read wrong, that is the reason — a field report with both values settles it. The other open points from the manuals are listed in usage §8 (XGT, "What the published manuals do not settle"). All of them are read only. HTTP and BACnet interfaces in an AID are recognised but not collected. Using KOSMO reference models KOSMO publishes AAS reference models per equipment type from the Korean manufacturing-data standardization programme at github.com/kosmo-AAS — the files are in kosmo-AAS/kasmo-AAS_Pubilc (the repository's own spelling). KOSMO submissions ask for metamodel V3.1; the published files themselves declare V3.0. Download the reference model for your machine from that repository. Open it in AAS Studio — the XML body is converted to JSON on import. Check against the KOSMO submission rules: filter the findings by L3, apply auto-fix where offered (usage §4-8). Fill in the machine's values — most findings are empty Property values the model leaves for you (usage §4-3). Download as V3.1 (usage §4-10). One-letter idShorts (Q, T, X …) are valid in V3.0 but not in V3.1, so the download window refuses them — rename them first. Of all errors, 64,357 are empty Property values (KOSMO-SME-4) and 146,106 are auto-fixable. Most frequent: KOSMO-SME-4 · AASd-121~128 · KOSMO-CD-2 · KOSMO-CD-4 · KOSMO-SME-5 Round trip 179 the same — every saved copy opens again Export as V3.1 156 written with 0 dropped values; 23 refused (one-letter idShorts). 33 of the 156 pass the official V3.1 schema — the rest fail on values in the source: empty lists (minItems 1), empty text, units or idShorts Every file, rule by rule: docs/kosmo-compat.md. License: that repository shows no license, so this repository does not include its files — it only links to them. Check the provider's terms before redistributing them. Things to know Authentication is opt-in. With neither accounts nor an API key the server only listens on the local machine. The OPC UA server (port 4840) requires an account and encryption (Sign / SignAndEncrypt). It is off by default; OPCUA_ALLOW_INSECURE=on restores the old unauthenticated port for isolated test networks only. Once people sign in, put HTTPS in front — see Caddyfile.example. In English, what stays as it was written is what comes from your own files (names, values) and the folder names of the submission bundle, which the submission format fixes. Server startup logs are Korean by default; set AAS_LANG=en for English. Report security problems through the channel in SECURITY.md, not a public issue. content_html_zh:
英语 · 韩语

Author, validate, serve and collect live values for AAS (Asset Administration Shell) — in one web app. Upload one machine's AASX, see exactly which rules it breaks, and fix what can be fixed in one step.

This used to take three tools. VEXPLOR AAS Studio brings the work together and is built so that people new to AAS can follow along.

Task Usual tool Here
Open · edit · export AASX AASX Package Explorer (desktop) In the browser, with findings and auto-fix
Serve AAS to other systems (Part 2 REST · registry) Eclipse BaSyx server The same server does it
Collect machine values · publish them by subscription Separate OPC UA client/server Collects per the AID in the AAS and publishes via an OPC UA server
Not affiliated with, and not derived from, the tools above — it combines the same jobs in one place.

新来的？ Click "Start with a sample" on the start screen to open a fully filled equipment file and a process structure.

Website: wace.me/en-platform-aas-studio

Docs: Usage · Install · Deployment & hosting · The 52 rules · Using it with Logic Studio — every document is also available in Korean.

Why

AAS is in place as a standard. Putting it into a factory is still work left outside the specification.

A review of ten years of AAS research (IEEE Access, 2025) names integration with existing machines and systems as a key challenge holding back adoption. Several studies point to the effort of building an AAS by hand, and the open tools are split into editors, servers and libraries, so collecting field values means mapping it yourself in configuration files. VEXPLOR AAS Studio lets software take on that work, so an AAS does not end as a document but becomes operating data with live values from the machines on the floor.

What people hit on the floor In VEXPLOR AAS Studio
Attaching to machines and PLCs that already run Collects from OPC UA, Modbus TCP and MQTT per the AID in the AAS, and reads S7, MELSEC (MC protocol) and LS ELECTRIC XGT PLCs directly — read only, a VEXPLOR extension binding. The remote collector sends outward only; PLC programs are not changed
Building an AAS by hand Start from a filled sample, fill values at once from tables or CSV; 52 rules point out problems and 19 fix them automatically
One tool per job Open, edit, check, Part 2 REST, field value collection and OPC UA publishing in one screen
Passing the standard, failing the receiver Checks the Korean receiving validator's (KOSMO Validator) business rules — semantic ID allow-list, mandatory submodels, package structure — before submission, and shows conflicts with the standard as a policy the user decides

There are real line deployments (Bosch Rexroth and others). They adopted AAS to end months of integration work whenever machines change — and they too report that creating the AAS itself is the first hurdle for many users. Evidence and sources: docs/background.md.

The receiving validator remains the only authority on acceptance. This tool is a pre-check.

它的作用
Open & edit Load AASX (JSON or XML), browse it as a tree, edit values, elements, submodels and concept descriptions. Fill many values at once from a submodel value table or from a CSV equipment list
Lint 52 rules in three layers — package structure (L1), metamodel constraints (L2), submission business rules (L3)
Auto-fix Preview the fixable findings (19 rules), choose, apply at once. Every relocation is recorded
报告 A printable HTML validation report
What to fill With the IDTA templates installed, every value row shows required · collected · optional, and "Show only what to fill" hides the rest
Undo & history One-step undo, and restore a submodel to an earlier point
Types and units Split a type file into units; when the type changes, review the differences line by line and pull only the lines you choose — values edited on site are never overwritten
Process bundles Company → line → process → equipment → part. Group machines into a process and export a submission bundle
Data collection Read live values from OPC UA · Modbus TCP · MQTT devices, and directly from S7, MELSEC (MC protocol) and LS ELECTRIC XGT PLCs — read only, a VEXPLOR extension binding not yet checked on real PLCs — addressed by the AID submodel inside the AAS. Each value shows whether it is live, stale or missing, and each machine gets a daily status bar (running · stopped · alarm). Add dozens of tags from one pattern
Standard API IDTA Part 2 REST API, so other systems can read the AAS held here
MES · ERP · CMMS integration A pull feed of every change and runtime event (CloudEvents), signed webhooks and MQTT, equipment / BOM / hierarchy / maintenance / document exports in JSON or CSV, ERP numbers kept next to the AASX, and server-side state, alarm, counter and threshold rules. A secure OPC UA server (accounts + encryption). See docs/integration.md
账户 Admin / editor / viewer, with an audit trail of who changed what
English & Korean, light & dark The interface and everything the server writes — findings, rule descriptions, the validation report, bundle README, errors — come in English or Korean. If you never choose, the browser language decides (Korean browser → Korean, anything else → English). Light and dark themes

What's new in 2.3 – 2.12

特征 发布 细节
Empty list elements in XML read as empty lists 2.12.1 A list closed with no items (<qualifiers />, <description />, a collection's <value /> …) was read as the empty string. In KOSMO's 179 public reference models the check then stopped part way in 45 files and a saved copy could not be opened again for 27; both are now 0. The empty list is kept as it was and reported by PKG-EMPTY-ARRAY (auto-fix). scripts/lint.mjs now checks each file by its own metamodel version and looks into subfolders. New guide: using KOSMO reference models with a file-by-file table
Range limits in tag hints 2.12.0 A Range element with the same semanticId as a tag's value now gives limits too — its min as lsl, its max as usl — so a receiver such as Logic Studio gets lower specification limits from the file. Limits from the KOSMO property pairs come first, ranges after; a tag may carry several of the same bound, each with its source, for a person to choose. No schema change. The KOSMO model files in use today hold no Range, so their hints are unchanged; for a lower limit, add a Range with the value's semanticId and an idShort different from the value's (integration)
LS ELECTRIC XGT, read directly 2.11.0 XGK · XGI · XGR · XGB PLCs with an FEnet module are read over the XGT dedicated protocol (TCP 2004) without a gateway — read only. Addresses are written as XG5000 shows them (D100, D100.3, P0001A, %MW100, %IX0.0.3). AID 1.1 has no XGT binding, so this is a VEXPLOR extension binding marked by our binding IRI. Built from LS ELECTRIC's published FEnet manual and tested against a test server built from it — not yet checked on a real PLC; please send a PLC field report. The server reads it with COLLECT=on, the remote collector from VEXPLOR Edge 1.3.0 — usage §8
XGT in the edge contract · PLC field report 2.11.0 The read list's protocol adds XGT; the contract stays vexplor.edge/1. Install them by release URL:

"@aas/aasx": "https://github.com/waceinc/vexplor-aas/releases/download/v2.12.1/aas-aasx-2.12.1.tgz"

Never by version number — the @aas scope on the public npm registry is not ours, so "@aas/core": "^2.0.0" would install whatever someone else publishes there. The tarballs point at each other by release URL, so one pinned URL is enough.

Using KOSMO reference models

KOSMO publishes AAS reference models per equipment type from the Korean manufacturing-data standardization programme at github.com/kosmo-AAS — the files are in kosmo-AAS/kasmo-AAS_Pubilc (the repository's own spelling). KOSMO submissions ask for metamodel V3.1; the published files themselves declare V3.0.

  1. Download the reference model for your machine from that repository.
  2. Open it in AAS Studio — the XML body is converted to JSON on import.
  3. Check against the KOSMO submission rules: filter the findings by L3, apply auto-fix where offered (usage §4-8).
  4. Fill in the machine's values — most findings are empty Property values the model leaves for you (usage §4-3).
  5. Download as V3.1 (usage §4-10). One-letter idShorts (Q, T, X …) are valid in V3.0 but not in V3.1, so the download window refuses them — rename them first.

要知道的事情

  • Authentication is opt-in. With neither accounts nor an API key the server only listens on the local machine.
  • The OPC UA server (port 4840) requires an account and encryption (Sign / SignAndEncrypt). It is off by default; OPCUA_ALLOW_INSECURE=on restores the old unauthenticated port for isolated test networks only.
  • Once people sign in, put HTTPS in front — see Caddyfile.example.
  • In English, what stays as it was written is what comes from your own files (names, values) and the folder names of the submission bundle, which the submission format fixes.
  • Server startup logs are Korean by default; set AAS_LANG=en for English.
  • Report security problems through the channel in SECURITY.md, not a public issue.
